blocks.content: Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code
Framer's free plan limits you to 2 published pages. For SpeedBlip, I needed designs for: a landing page, a dashboard page, a history page, and a settings page.

The workaround: I put everything on one Framer project as stacked sections, not separate pages. The landing page was one section, the dashboard was another, and so on. In Framer, I could scroll through all the designs in one view, and I used them purely as a visual reference - not as a handoff file.

This is worth noting because it illustrates a mindset that matters for rapid building: you are not trying to produce a perfect design artifact. You are producing enough visual clarity to write a good Claude Code prompt. The wireframe's job is done the moment you have answered "what does this screen look like and how does it behave?"
Below is the prompt used to generate the initial layout reference.

"Design a modern light-theme web app called PingPulse — a real-time internet speed monitor for developers. Use soft white (#F8FAFC) as the background, green (#22C55E) as the primary accent color, and Inter as the font. All cards should use a glassmorphism style — semi-transparent white backgrounds, backdrop blur, subtle white borders, and soft shadows. The design has two pages. Page 1 is the landing page with: a hero section featuring a bold headline 'Know your speed. 
Before it slows you down.', a subheadline, a green CTA button, and a preview of the speed gauge UI; a 3-step how it works section; a features section with 3 icon cards; a FAQ section; and a footer. Page 2 is the app page with three full-height sections using a sticky top navigation with anchor links: first section is the Dashboard with a circular animated speed gauge, three glassmorphism stat cards showing download speed, upload speed, and ping, and a small line chart; second section is History with a full-width line chart and date filter; third section is Settings with a bandwidth threshold input, test interval dropdown, and a push notification toggle. Make everything responsive across mobile, tablet, and desktop. Keep the design spacious, minimal, and premium."
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
